newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas down late but still in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas down late but still in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, pressured by reports of a softer cash market, remained broadly lower late Thursday in moderate activity, but prices were still holding recent ranges, sources said.
At 1435 EST, March was still down by 4.1 cents at $1.975 per million British thermal units, while April was 6.4 cents lower at $1.94. Most others were down by 0.1 to 4.9 cents.

"Cash started down but came back a little. It's (March) well offered above $2 but well bid in the low-$1.90s," said a Texas trader, adding the gap between physical and futures prices had narrowed significantly ahead of the March expiry.
NYMEX March Hub natgas goes off the board Monday.

While the market could rally on short covering ahead of the March expiration, traders said forecasts for normal to above-normal U.S. weather into early March were likely to limit any upside move, particularly with eastern storage running about 50 percent above year-ago levels.
"Eastern LDCs (utilities) are not returning phone calls. They have too much inventory and they know the gas will be out there if they need it," said a Houston-based marketer.
AGA data released Wednesday showed that overall U.S. gas inventories were still 14.5 percent over year-ago, with eastern stocks 233 bcf, or 51 percent, above last year.
Traders now pegged near-support in March in the $1.93 area, then at Tuesday's low of $1.85 and at the contract low of $1.749. Resistance was at $2.08-2.09 and then $2.25-2.30.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices eased slightly Thursday to the high-$1.80s to $1.90 area. Midcon pipes lost similar ground to the low-$1.70s. New York city gate gas also was talked modestly lower at $2.15.
NYMEX said an estimated 13,470 Hub contracts traded as of 1135 EST.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas were untraded at 1200 EST.
On the KCBT, March slipped eight cents to $1.63, while deferreds were down by one to four cents. The East/West spread widened by 3.9 cents to 34.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
